Anna / Mina — quick legal summary for the TIA appendix:

- SCC applicability: For MedNorth as a data exporter in the EU and Redwood as processor, standard EU SCCs (controller-processor or processor-processor depending on the flow) apply for any transfers to third countries. We recommend the modular processor-to-processor Addendum plus the supplementary measures narrative (encryption-at-rest, key residency, strict access controls).

- DPA clause snippet (short): "Redwood shall ensure that any transfers of personal data outside the EEA are subject to appropriate safeguards, including execution of the EU Standard Contractual Clauses and implementation of technical and organisational measures to protect data in transit and at rest." (See attached doc for full wording and options).

- Mitigations we typically propose in TIAs:
  * Encryption at-rest with keys tied to the EU region where feasible;
  * Role-based access controls and just-in-time privilege elevation for restores;
  * Logging and time-bound access for any restore operations;
  * Pseudonymization of identifiers used in operational logs where possible;
  * Contractual commitments on subprocessors and a right to audit.

I attached a short DPA snippet and an example mitigations paragraph you can paste into the TIA. If MedNorth requires EU-only storage of backups (no cross-border replication at all), that's feasible as a configuration option for enterprise customers but we'll need an explicit contract appendix and possibly a small operational uplift for DR runbooks.

Attachment: DPA_snippet_SCCs_v2.docx

Hi all — technical details below (EU tenant behavior):

1) Backup location and replication
- For hosted EU tenants, automated backups (block snapshots) are stored in the customer-designated EU region by default (we use multi-zone within the region for redundancy).
- Cross-region replication to non-EU regions is NOT automatic. We only enable cross-region replication for customers that opt into a global DR configuration in the Redwood Console (explicit feature flag + contract).
- When cross-region replication is enabled, snapshots are encrypted and transferred over TLS; encryption keys remain in the originating region unless the customer explicitly requests cross-region KMS key usage.

2) Encryption & KMS
- Snapshots and nightly backups are encrypted with AES-256. For Dedicated and Private deployments customers can supply a CMK (customer-managed key) in their cloud KMS; for hosted customers we store KMS keys in the EU region for EU tenants by default.

3) Restore procedures & logs
- Restore logs contain resource identifiers and operation metadata but do NOT include raw patient data by default. The restore process mounts encrypted volumes and data is mounted only transiently on worker nodes.
- Operational audit logs capture the user id performing the restore, timestamp, and job id. Where a restore references a specific record id (internal object id), we recommend pseudonymizing before exporting logs for legal review.
- Access to perform restores is restricted to a small set of SREs under RBAC; restores require a ticket and are recorded in the audit trail. Temporary elevated access is time-limited and logged.

4) Retention and retention-on-restore
- Backups retention: default 30 days for snapshots; can be extended per contract. Restore artifacts (temporary volumes) are destroyed immediately after validation; meta-logs retained for 365 days unless customer requests shorter retention.

If MedNorth needs EU-only guarantees (no exports of encrypted snapshots outside the EU), we can provide a contractual guarantee + technical configuration to prevent enabling cross-region replication for their tenant. That option is typically scoped to Dedicated or enterprise-hosted tier due to operational constraints.

I can also share the restore runbook (redacted) and the permissions matrix used during drills — these are internal docs, so we'd provide a tailored extract for legal review.

—Vivek

Hi Anna — summary and next steps below. Thanks for patience while we pulled the details together.

Summary (for your TIA appendix):
- Backup residency: EU-hosted MedNorth tenants have snapshots stored in the customer EU region by default; cross-region replication to non-EU is opt-in only.
- Encryption & keys: AES-256 encrypted at rest. For hosted EU tenants, KMS keys are stored in the EU region by default; Dedicated/Private customers may supply CMKs.
- Restore logs & PII: Restore logs do not contain raw patient data by default; they include metadata and object ids. We recommend pseudonymizing identifiers in exported logs submitted as evidence.
- Operational controls: restores require a ticket, are restricted to RBAC-approved SREs, and elevated access is time-limited and logged.
- Contractual path: we will provide the EU SCCs addendum + the DPA snippet (attached) and can add an explicit appendix to prevent cross-border replication if MedNorth requires an EU-only guarantee (scope & pricing discussion needed).

Action items:
1) I attached the DPA snippet Rishi mentioned and a blank TIA_spreadsheet_template.xlsx to capture the remaining required fields.
2) If you want EU-only persistence for backups (hard block on cross-region replication), please confirm and we will prepare an appendix and an operational plan; we estimate a 3–4 week lead time to lock operational procedures and validation tests.
3) If helpful, we can set a 30-min call this week to walk through the TIA worksheet.
